title: Single-select — one correct answer
description: Three single-select Quiz widgets back to back, each with a different number of options and an explanation that reveals on submit.

data.markdown: A **single-select** Quiz renders a question, a list of options, and a Submit button. Exactly one option is correct; the user picks one and submits. After submitting, the widget reveals a per-question explanation and locks the form. The section is marked done in `progress.json` only on a fully-correct submission.

data.question: True or false: a single-select Quiz allows the user to pick more than one option per attempt.
options: True — the user may select any subset of options.
False — single-select means exactly one selected option per attempt.
data.explanation: Single-select means radio-button semantics: clicking a new option deselects the previous one. Use the `multiSelect: true` mode if you need to allow multiple selections.

data.question: Which of these widget types renders Markdown narration with KaTeX math and `:::callout{type=...}` directives?
data.explanation: Theory is the Markdown-narration widget. Quiz is the assessment widget you are filling in right now, Code runs Python in a Pyodide worker, and DataTable renders sortable/filterable tabular data.

data.question: After a correct submission, the Quiz widget…
options: Auto-navigates to the next lesson without confirmation.
Reveals the per-question explanation and marks the section done in `progress.json`.
Re-runs the lesson's Pyodide setup code.
Posts the answer to a remote leaderboard.
Resets the form so the user can try a different answer.
data.explanation: On a fully-correct submission the explanation panel appears AND the section's `done: true` flag is persisted via PATCH `/api/progress`. There is no auto-navigation, no remote scoring, and the form locks rather than resetting.
